key_insight: An open-source hardware/software toolkit turns RHEED into an agent-ready, automated measurement and analysis stack for thin-film growth control.
engineering_relevance: It lowers the barrier to autonomous synthesis by standardizing electron-optics control, alignment, and quantitative analysis through operator-friendly and AI-accessible interfaces.
method: Programmable RHEED electron-optics control on a pulsed laser deposition system
Automated beam alignment, rocking-curve acquisition, and training-free crystallographic azimuthal alignment
Shared GUI/API plus MCP server and extensible adapters for analysis and simulation integration
evidence_signal: The toolkit was demonstrated on a pulsed laser deposition system, where an agent used natural-language requests to select, configure, and run quantitative RHEED analyses.
watch_item: Autonomous performance depends on reliable hardware calibration, adapter quality, and careful validation of new community-developed analysis methods before deployment.
paper_title: An Open-Source Hardware and Software Toolkit to Enable Agentic RHEED-Guided Thin-Film Synthesis
